realign.note: AOTInductor's aligned-input fast path is 16 bytes and is the compiler's constant, not a knob. A misaligned feed runs correctly and copies per call, so alignment never moves admission; it only earns a staging buffer.

recast.note: The only dtype normalization. Value-preserving: float32 represents every integer below 2**24 exactly, and it is the op the traced graph's own first node performs on that input. It is also the only normalization that moves ADMISSION.

note: Which declared graph class serves one call, and how far the ones that do not sit from it. torchcg owns CallIngress identity; these vectors own what a serve host DOES with several of them. The reference implementation is torchcg.selection and tests/test_selection.py replays every row through it. A change to a selection implementation that is not a change to this file is a fleet that disagrees about admission, which is invisible until it serves wrong. OUT OF SCOPE by construction: eager fallback, sticky de-arm, shape-growth reporting, event emission and refusal wording are host policy; the candidate set is the host's and selection never asks why a class is absent.

vectors.name: one_class_admits
vectors.note: The base case: exactly one class admits, the symbolic batch binds, and no feed needs normalizing. Admission is the ABSENCE of a miss, so an admitted selection carries no ranking at all.

vectors.name: recast_admits_an_integer_scalar
vectors.note: An int64 rank-0 timestep against a float32-specialized scalar. The ddim/dpmpp/unipc sampler families end set_timesteps in .to(int64) while the euler families present float32, so refusing this would refuse a class that covers the call in every other respect. The recast is the ONE normalization that moves admission.

vectors.name: recast_targets_float64_too
vectors.note: float64 is the second permitted recast target; the reason names the exact dtype pair, never just 'recast'.

vectors.name: recast_never_targets_bfloat16
vectors.note: bf16 has 8 mantissa bits and would round timestep 999 to 1000. That is a numeric change, not a normalization, so the class refuses on dtype and the call is a total miss.

vectors.name: recast_is_rank_zero_only
vectors.note: An integer tensor OF timesteps is not a scalar timestep. Recasting a ranked feed would be a dtype conversion of real data, so the class refuses on both dtype and rank — and two misses sort behind one.

vectors.name: realign_does_not_move_admission
vectors.note: diffusers hands the denoiser timesteps[i], a scalar VIEW at an odd element offset. AOTInductor runs it correctly and copies it on every call, so alignment is a PERFORMANCE fact: the class still admits, and the plan says to stage the feed once.

vectors.name: non_contiguous_feeds_realign
vectors.note: A non-contiguous feed takes the same staging path under its own reason. Contiguity is checked before the address, so a feed that is both reports the layout, which is the fact that explains the other.

vectors.name: recast_subsumes_realign
vectors.note: A feed that needs both gets ONE normalization, the recast. A recast implies a staged copy into the declared dtype, and that buffer is aligned by construction — staging twice would pay the copy twice for a feed that ends in the same buffer either way.

vectors.name: the_plan_is_in_position_order
vectors.note: Several normalized feeds are planned in declared POSITION order, never in the order the host happened to resolve them: a host that applies the plan top to bottom must never wonder which slot it is staging.

vectors.name: an_excluded_input_routes_to_the_adapter_class
vectors.note: The call carries lora_a, so the branchless class REFUSES it — a class fed an adapter it does not declare would return the base model and look correct. The class that declares the pair admits.

vectors.name: a_missing_input_is_the_only_miss
vectors.note: The call does not carry text_embeds at all, and its sample is float32 besides. Nothing further about the class is measurable once a declared input is absent, so the report is exactly one miss at the deepest rung — not a list that invites a reader to fix the dtype first.

vectors.name: a_non_tensor_feed_ranks_rather_than_crashes
vectors.note: A declared input presented as something with no shape (a Python float, a list, None) is a miss, not an exception. The walk continues to the remaining inputs so the report still says everything it can.

vectors.name: the_closest_class_is_the_one_whose_dims_match
vectors.note: THE ranking case. Three classes refuse a 64x64 call whose scalar is bfloat16: the base class matches every declared dimension and disagrees about one scalar fact, the hi-res class does not fit the graph at all, and the adapter class cannot even find its inputs. Listing them in iteration order buries the one a reader needs, so the shallow rung sorts first.

vectors.name: fewer_complaints_wins_at_the_same_rung
vectors.note: Two classes share their shallowest complaint. The sorted rung tuple makes a prefix sort before its extension, so the class with fewer complaints is closer — 'one dtype disagreement' beats 'one dtype disagreement and two dims'.

vectors.name: an_exact_tie_breaks_on_the_class_name
vectors.note: Two classes at the same distance with the same misses. The tie breaks on the class NAME ascending, so a host that offers its candidates in a different order still prints the same closest class.

vectors.name: a_symbolic_dim_outside_its_range_refuses
vectors.note: batch=16 is outside the declared inclusive range [1, 8]. A range violation and a static-dim mismatch share a rung because both say the same thing: the call does not fit this graph.

vectors.name: one_symbol_must_take_one_value
vectors.note: batch binds to 2 on sample and 3 on text_embeds. range_constraints cannot express this, but the graph requires it, so a call that is individually in range on both is still outside the declared envelope. The first binding wins and names the input that disagreed with it.

vectors.name: two_admitting_classes_are_a_defect
vectors.note: The declaration failed to discriminate two graph classes by ingress. That is a defect to surface, never a coin to flip: an outcome that picked one would serve a different graph on a different pod for the same request.

vectors.name: an_empty_candidate_set_is_a_total_miss
vectors.note: A host with nothing armed yet asks the same question and gets the same answer shape. Why the set is empty — nothing compiled, everything de-armed, a cold boot — is the host's knowledge, never selection's.

vectors.name: an_excluded_input_no_class_declares_is_a_total_miss
vectors.note: The call carries an adapter and the only candidate refuses adapters. The refusal names the excluded input, at its own rung: a routing disagreement is a wrong-class fact, deeper than a scalar disagreement and shallower than a shape one.
